description: Which published pages Google has never shown anyone. Reads the domain's sitemap, compares it against every page that earned at least one impression in the window, and returns the silent ones grouped by URL prefix so a whole dead section is obvious at a glance. This is usually the fastest 'here is what is wrong' a site can get: a library where half the URLs have never surfaced is not a ranking problem, it is pages published against demand that was never verified. Note the two causes it CANNOT separate — never indexed, versus indexed but never competitive. Confirm the difference with URL Inspection in Search Console before acting. Fetches the sitemap over HTTP from the domain itself. Requires a paid plan (Starter+).

days.description: Window for 'earned an impression'. Default 90 — use the widest window the property has.

domain.description: Bare domain, e.g. 'example.com'. Its public sitemap is fetched over HTTP.

limit.description: Max silent URLs listed. Default 100 (counts are always complete).

name: gsc_coverage_gap
